item.title: Drainage work to close Birchwood Street in King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Drainage work to close Birchwood Street in King’s Lynn
Norfolk County Council is set to begin essential drainage work on Birchwood Street in King’s Lynn. Starting on or around Thursday, November 19, the project involves digging trial holes and is expected to last five days, with completion scheduled for November 25, weather permitting.
The road will be closed to traffic for the duration of the works. While access for residents and businesses will be maintained from one end of the street, there may be temporary restrictions directly outside individual properties. Motorists are being asked to remove all vehicles from parking areas along the road to ensure safety. Emergency services have been notified of the planned closure.

item.title: Looking back at local news from November 2013 and 2014
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Looking back at local news from November 2013 and 2014
We are taking a look back at stories from across the region during November in 2013 and 2014. Notable events included the 40th anniversary of the Dersingham Scout and Guide headquarters and the 50th anniversary of the North Lynn Methodist Church. In King’s Lynn, the first phase of the Hillington Square regeneration was completed, and the town saw the opening of The Gatehouse pub. Other highlights from the period included the Christmas lights switch-on, fundraising efforts at the Bespak factory for Movember, and the return of a restored World War I medal to a local family. Additionally, the Sandringham Flower Show announced a record donation of £50,000 to various charities.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
New management team takes over historic King’s Lynn pub
The Lattice House on Chapel Street in King’s Lynn is under new management. Owner Daniel High has appointed Shannon Durrant to lead the historic venue, which dates back to the late 1400s. Mr Durrant, who has extensive experience in the West Norfolk hospitality sector, is leading a team of chefs and front-of-house staff.
The pub has introduced a new menu featuring pub classics, pizzas, and Thursday night curries, alongside a new cocktail selection. Future plans for the venue include the introduction of a gravity-fed bar for ales and beers. Mr Durrant says his goal is to create a welcoming atmosphere and build a sustainable business that the local community can be proud of.

item.description:

Firework displays scheduled across West Norfolk this week
Residents across West Norfolk have several firework displays to look forward to this week. Events begin on Thursday, November 5, at the North Wootton Scout and Guide Headquarters, with gates opening at 5pm. On Friday, November 6, King’s Lynn hosts the Fawkes in The Walks event, featuring live entertainment from 6pm and a choreographed display at 8pm.
The weekend continues on Saturday, November 7, with the Hunstanton and District Round Table’s 50th anniversary clifftop display, and a two-part event at the Denver playing fields. Those planning to attend should check local websites for ticket information and specific entry requirements, as arrangements vary between locations.

Power restored following North Lynn building fire
Four fire crews were called to a building blaze on Coulton Close in North Lynn yesterday evening. Firefighters from King’s Lynn, Terrington, and Sandringham attended the scene after the alarm was raised at 7:36pm.
To ensure safety during the operation, UK Power Networks isolated electricity supplies to 108 households at 8:29pm. Power was successfully restored to all but one of those properties by 10:05pm. Crews remained on site until the incident was concluded at 1:51am this morning.

Series of convictions at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court
A range of cases were heard at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court last Thursday. Several individuals appeared before the bench for driving offences, including drink and drug-driving. Among those sentenced were Oliver Saunders of Stoke Ferry, who received a 12-month driving ban for being six times over the cocaine limit, and Kevin Sherman of Necton, who was disqualified for 15 months for drink-driving.
The court also dealt with various theft and public order offences. These included a shoplifting case involving 20 bottles of whisky, a man pleading guilty to cultivating cannabis, and a case involving threatening behaviour at a restaurant in King’s Lynn. Several defendants were issued fines and court costs, with some sentencing hearings adjourned until later this year.

item.title: Power restored following North Lynn building fire
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Power restored following North Lynn building fire
Four fire crews were called to a building blaze on Coulton Close in North Lynn yesterday evening. Firefighters from King’s Lynn, Terrington, and Sandringham arrived at the scene following a report at 7:36pm.
To ensure safety, UK Power Networks engineers isolated electricity supplies to 108 households at 8:29pm. Power was restored to all but one of those properties by 10:05pm. Crews remained on site using hose reel and main jets to tackle the fire, with the incident officially concluded at 1:51am this morning.
